messages.subject: Issues with returnFileNamesMissingTags in getSpeciesImages
parts:
Hi all,
I'm attempting to simply start my workflow by using the getSpeciesImages command, and am unable to even run this first script.
I have 60 folders of photos that I need to copy images of only a single species, so my initial code looks like this:

species_to_copy <- "Pseudantechinus_mimulus"

pmimulus_records <- getSpeciesImages(species_to_copy,
                                     inDir = wd_images_raw,
                                     outDir = "E:/Masters/05_2018/species_folders",
                                     createStationSubfolders = FALSE,
                                     IDfrom = "metadata",
                                     metadataSpeciesTag = "species",
                                     metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|"
)

When I run this it gets through reading 19 folders and spits out the following error message:

Error in isTRUE(returnFileNamesMissingTags) : 
  argument "returnFileNamesMissingTags" is missing, with no default

If I attempt to add the following to my code, with either TRUE or FALSE ...

mimulus_records <- getSpeciesImages(species_to_copy,
                                     inDir = wd_images_raw,
                                     outDir = "E:/Masters/05_2018/species_folders",
                                     createStationSubfolders = FALSE,
                                     IDfrom = "metadata",
                                     metadataSpeciesTag = "species",
                                     metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                     returnFileNamesMissingTags = FALSE
)

... I then get an error message telling me:

Error in getSpeciesImages(species = species_to_copy, inDir = wd_images_raw,  : 
  unused argument (returnFileNamesMissingTags = FALSE)

To my novice eye, it looks like the code requires me to use returnFileNamesMissingTags but at the same time doesn't use it and stops the script from running.

Am I missing something quite simple here?

Thanks,
Jarrad
